# LG Connections

There are (at least) 3 different variants of the R32 ThermaV monobloc heatpump  **series 3**, which has case 1 and case 2 types, and the later **series 4**.

In all cases the connection required is to the 3rd party controller.  These terminals are clearly marked within the LG unit.  Ensure the wiring to terminals A and B is documented to maintain correct polarity with the Modbus master. A 120 Ω (0.25 W) termination resistor should be installed across these terminals to mitigate electrical interference. While short cable runs may function without it, installing the resistor is recommended for signal integrity. Note that Modbus utilizes differential signaling; therefore, a dedicated ground connection is typically not required.

From the LG installation manual the relevant terminal block connections are shown for each model.

## Post LG Electrical Interfacing

The installer must take note of the A and B connections that have been made, and to ensure that the other end of the cable those wires are not shorting out.  These A and B connections will subsequently be made to the modbusTCP adapter.  Therefore it is important that any colour coding of cables that have been used for A and B are duly noted for subsequent connection.  Filling in this short table would be helpful.

| LG Model  (Series 3 case 1, 2 or Series 4\) |  |  |
| :---- | ----- | :---- |
| LG Terminal  | Modbus | Cable Colour Code |
|  | A |  |
|  | B |  |

# LG DIP Switch Settings

With the physical connection made to the LG then the next step is to ensure that DIP switches in the unit have been set such that the LG will be acting as a modbus slave device, and using the standard modbus protocol.

## Series 3

![][image10]

![][image11]

For SW1 both DIP switch 1 and 2 must be set to the ON position, which is likely opposite to the default settings.  The orientation of this diagram is actually inverted to how the installer will see the board \- so SW1 wll be to the mid-upper right as opposed to the mid-lower left as shown here.

\*Note: It isn’t known whether the PCB layout is different between the case 1 and case 2 variants of the series 3 ThermaV.

## Series 4

![][image12]

![][image13]

Similar to the series 3, for SW1 both DIP switch 1 and 2 must be set to the ON position,  which is likely opposite to the default settings.  And also the orientation of this diagram is actually inverted to how the installer will see the board \- so SW1 wll be to the mid left as opposed to the mid right as shown here.

There are videos available on YouTube that show modbus connectivity for ThermaV’s, e.g.

Homely (series 4\) : [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=js7nFTKm5aM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=js7nFTKm5aM)  
Rod McBain (series 3\) : [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xuj2YFZ5zME](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xuj2YFZ5zME)

# LG Controller Setting

After the electrical connections have been made to the LG and the DIP switches set to their correct positions then the unit should be re-started and a check made that the unit is operating normally.  The LG controller will still be able to communicate with the outdoor unit and control operation as before.

Before interfacing any modbus master device to the LG, then its slave address must be set.

## Series 3

Probably using software revision 3.0.5.3 to 3.0.5.6, the menu option is in the installer settings:

![][image14]

The modbus address can be set to that expected by the master controller.  A sensible value would be 09 as this is probably not used by other devices on the bus.

## Series 4

The modbus slave address is set in a series 4 controller, i.e. using software revision 3.0.6.4 onwards, then the installer menu option is:

![][image15]

The modbus address can be set to that expected by the master controller.  A sensible value would be 09 as this is probably not used by other devices on the bus.
